Risk: Shadow AI use with company data
Description: Staff use personal or free AI accounts and unapproved tools for work, putting company or client data outside company control.
Planned treatment: Publish the Acceptable Use Policy and approved tool list; provide an approved alternative; use web filtering or monitoring for unapproved AI sites; train staff.

Risk: Confidential data entered into an approved tool beyond its permitted classification
Description: Users paste Confidential or Restricted data into a tool only approved for lower classifications.
Planned treatment: Apply data rules by classification; enable DLP or browser controls where available; anonymise before use; refresher training.

Risk: Vendor trains on our data or retains prompts too long
Description: AI vendor uses customer inputs for model training or keeps prompts and outputs longer than needed.
AI use case or system: Any AI vendor or embedded AI feature
Planned treatment: Use the Vendor Review Checklist (A1, A2); choose business plans with training opt-out; record terms in the vendor file; set retention to the minimum.

Risk: Prompt injection through emails, documents or web content
Description: Hidden or malicious instructions in content processed by an AI tool cause it to leak data or take unintended actions.
AI use case or system: AI assistants that read email, documents or web pages
Planned treatment: Treat all processed content as untrusted; limit tool permissions; require human approval for actions; test with injection scenarios.

Risk: Excessive agency of AI assistants and agents
Description: AI agents hold broad permissions (email, files, tickets, code, payments) and act on wrong or manipulated output.
Planned treatment: Least privilege for every connector; human approval for irreversible or external actions; separate service accounts; log agent actions.

Risk: Inaccurate or fabricated AI output used in deliverables
Description: Hallucinated facts, citations, figures or advice appear in client work, reports or decisions.
Planned treatment: Mandatory human review and source checks before release; keep an audit trail for client-facing work; disclose AI use where required.

Risk: Intellectual property and copyright exposure
Description: AI output infringes third-party rights, or company IP is exposed or ownership of output is unclear.
Planned treatment: Check output ownership and indemnity in vendor terms; avoid copying others' work; keep a record of significant AI-generated assets.

Risk: Compromised AI vendor, plugin, extension, model or MCP server
Description: A malicious or vulnerable component in the AI supply chain exposes data or runs unauthorised code.
AI use case or system: Plugins, browser extensions, connectors, third-party models
Planned treatment: Approved list for extensions and connectors; review publishers and permissions; pin versions; remove unused integrations.

Risk: Poisoned or untrusted data in knowledge bases or fine-tuning data
Description: Incorrect or manipulated documents in a retrieval or training source skew answers or hide malicious content.
Planned treatment: Control who can add sources; review content before indexing; respect document permissions; monitor answer quality.

Risk: System prompts, keys or internal context exposed
Description: Credentials, confidential instructions or internal context embedded in prompts or configurations are revealed to users or attackers.
Planned treatment: Never store secrets in prompts; use a secrets manager; assume prompts can be extracted; review custom assistant configurations.

Risk: Runaway usage and cost
Description: Uncontrolled API or agent usage causes unexpected charges or service exhaustion.
Planned treatment: Set spend caps, rate limits and usage alerts; review invoices monthly; require approval for new API keys.

Risk: Unvalidated AI output used in code, commands or systems
Description: AI-generated code, queries or scripts are run or rendered without review and introduce vulnerabilities or damage.
Planned treatment: Code review and security testing for AI-written code; sandbox before running; block direct execution from chat to production.

Risk: AI-enabled social engineering and deepfake impersonation
Description: Attackers use AI voice, video or text to impersonate executives, suppliers or clients and trigger payments or access changes.
AI use case or system: Finance, HR, IT service desk, client communications
Planned treatment: Out-of-band verification for payment and access changes; awareness training with AI examples; reporting route for suspicious messages.

Risk: Biased or unfair AI-assisted decisions about people
Description: AI used in hiring, performance, credit or pricing decisions produces discriminatory outcomes or unlawful automated decisions.
Planned treatment: Prohibit solely automated decisions about people; require human review; assess impact and document the rationale before any such use.

Risk: Regulatory or contractual non-compliance
Description: AI use breaches data protection law, AI-specific rules (such as EU AI Act duties), sector rules or client contract terms.
Planned treatment: Maintain a list of applicable rules; check client contracts; legal review of the policy; keep training and decision records.

Risk: No AI inventory or accountable owner
Description: AI features embedded in SaaS tools and employee-adopted tools are not tracked, and nobody owns the risk.
AI use case or system: All AI tools and embedded AI features
Planned treatment: Create the approved AI tool register; name an owner per tool; review SaaS settings for default-on AI features quarterly.

Risk: Insufficient logging and monitoring of AI use
Description: Without logs it is not possible to investigate misuse, data exposure or agent actions.
Planned treatment: Enable audit logs; retain them to a defined period; review usage reports at least quarterly; include AI in incident response.

Risk: Over-reliance and automation bias
Description: Staff accept AI output without challenge, and skills or verification habits erode over time.
Planned treatment: Verification rules in the policy; spot checks on AI-assisted work; training on typical failure modes.

Risk: Meeting recorders and transcription tools capture sensitive conversations
Description: AI note-takers join or record meetings without consent, capturing privileged, confidential or personal discussions.
Planned treatment: Approve one meeting tool; obtain participant consent; disable auto-join bots; restrict sharing of transcripts.

Risk: AI tool account takeover
Description: Accounts without SSO or MFA are compromised, exposing chat history and connected data.
Planned treatment: Enforce SSO and MFA; ban shared accounts; review connected apps; reset sessions on staff exit.

Risk: Vendor outage, price change or model retirement
Description: A critical AI dependency becomes unavailable, expensive or changes behaviour, disrupting processes.
Planned treatment: Document manual fallback; avoid single-vendor dependency for critical processes; review contract change terms; keep exportable data.
